issues.legal_issue: A financial corporation cannot recover a debt through a separate state public-money recovery procedure when that procedure is not among the routes preserved by the overriding debt-recovery law.
material_facts: A financial corporation initiated proceedings to recover alleged loan dues under a state public-money recovery law after the borrower allegedly defaulted.

The debt-recovery law gave its provisions overriding effect over inconsistent laws, while its savings clause named specified enactments, including the state financial corporations law, but not the public-money recovery law.
The public-money recovery procedure was a separate mode and was not a mode of recovery under the saved state financial corporations law.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings under the state public-money recovery law were not maintainable and were quashed. The financial corporation remained free to pursue any recovery action legally available under the debt-recovery law or the state financial corporations law.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 17 and 18 of the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 vest exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate applications for debts due to banks and financial institutions in the Tribunal. Section 34(1) gives that Act overriding effect, subject to the enactments specified in Section 34(2), which is additional to and not in derogation of the State Financial Corporations Act, 1951. Section 32G of the State Financial Corporations Act provides a recovery mode for amounts due to a financial corporation, while Section 3 of the Uttar Pradesh Public Moneys (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1972 provides a separate route. Under Allahabad Bank v. Canara Bank, the Tribunal’s exclusive jurisdiction concerns adjudication of liability; the Court held that the savings for the State Financial Corporations Act did not preserve the separate route under the Uttar Pradesh Act.

predicates.financial_recovery_proceeding: A financial institution initiated a proceeding to recover a debt allegedly owed by a borrower after default.
predicates.overriding_recovery_law: The governing recovery law gives its provisions priority over inconsistent laws, subject to a defined list of preserved enactments.
predicates.invoked_route_is_outside_preserved_modes: The creditor invoked a separate recovery route that is outside the routes preserved by the governing recovery law.

issues.definition: When a financial institution seeks recovery through a route outside those preserved by an overriding recovery law, recovery through that route is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot add an omitted recovery route to a statutory exception by interpretation when the statutory language is plain and no clear necessity to do so appears from the statute.
material_facts: The financial corporation argued that the omitted public-money recovery route should be treated as covered by the statutory savings clause.
The savings clause expressly identified certain enactments but did not identify the public-money recovery law.
The Court found no basis in the statutory text for treating the omission as one that could be supplied through interpretation.
issues.conclusion: The omitted recovery route could not be read into the statutory exception by applying the doctrine of casus omissus.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the rule that courts interpret legislation but do not legislate, and that a casus omissus cannot ordinarily be supplied unless there is clear necessity apparent within the statute. It relied on Lenigh Valley Coal Co. v. Yensavage, Union of India v. Filip Tiago De Gama, D.R. Venkatchalam v. Deputy Transport Commissioner, Rishabh Agro Industries Ltd. v. P.N.B. Capital Services Ltd., N. Narasimhaiah v. State of Karnataka, State of Karnataka v. Nanjudaiah, Artemiou v. Procopiou, and Luke v. I.R.C. The statute must be read as a whole, but that principle does not permit adding words where the language is plain and unambiguous.

predicates.court_is_asked_to_supply_an_omission: A party asks the court to treat an unmentioned category as included in a statutory exception.
predicates.statutory_language_is_plain_and_unambigu: The words used in the relevant statutory text are plain and unambiguous.
predicates.no_clear_necessity_appears_within_the_st: The statute itself does not disclose a clear necessity to include the omitted category.

issues.definition: When a court is asked to include an omitted category, the text is plain, and the statute shows no clear necessity for inclusion, the category cannot be added by interpretation.
